messages:
Maya (Support): Heads-up — BrightHealth opened an escalation. After the model bump yesterday they say outputs are "too compact" and skip clarifying Qs. Two request ids: req-0a3f, req-0a3e. Can ML/SRE triage? :thinking:

Liam (ML Eng): which model/version was promoted and when? any change to sampling defaults or prompt-wrapping?

deploy-bot: rollout complete - model-catalog/model-v2.2 promoted to production at 2026-03-15T18:42:09Z (canary -> 100%).

Maya (Support): Customer provided before/after snippets. Prompt they used: `Help me write an email to a vendor to request pricing details for volume discounts.`
Before (v2.1):
```
Hi — I can help draft that. Quick question: is the tone formal or casual? Also do you want to include any pricing targets?
[Then a 4-paragraph email with polite intro and closing]
```
After (v2.2):
```
Here’s a short email you can send:
Please send your best volume pricing.
Thanks.
```

Liam (ML Eng): thanks, that's useful. Maya, can you paste the exact API payload they sent (model param + temperature/top_p/max_tokens) and SDK version?

Maya (Support): They called hosted API via node-sdk v1.4.2 using `model: "redwood-model-v2.2"`, `temperature: 0.0`, `max_tokens: 200`, `stream: false`. Their curl reproduced call: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-model-v2.2","input":"Help me write an email to a vendor to request pricing details for volume discounts.","temperature":0.0,"max_tokens":200}'
```

Jenna (SRE): we did push model-v2.2 yesterday during the 18:30 deploy window. No infra flags changed, but runtime default kernel was switched to `fast-det` to shave latency. I’m pulling inference logs for req-0a3f/0a3e now.

Jenna (SRE): logs snippet for req-0a3f:
```
[2026-03-15T18:43:12Z] req-0a3f model=redwood-model-v2.2 kernel=fast-det quant=8bit latency_ms=112.3 user=brighthealth
[2026-03-15T18:43:12Z] prompt_wrap_applied=normalize_roles=true system_trim=enabled
[2026-03-15T18:43:12Z] sampling_backend=deterministic_pool method=beam_fallback=false
```

Liam (ML Eng): interesting — two things to investigate: 1) `system_trim=enabled` could remove polite scaffolding if we tightened wrapper heuristics, 2) switching kernel/sampling backend may affect decode heuristics at low temperature (temp=0.0 makes model deterministic and concise).

Maya (Support): Customer insists behavior is worse than "deterministic" — they lost the clarifying question step we used to see. They want either revert or a config to restore previous verbosity.

Liam (ML Eng): quick mitigations we can suggest: set temperature >= 0.5 for more elaboration, or enable `safe_prompt_expansion=true` (internal flag) which restores extra clarifying probes. I can also run a local eval comparing v2.1 vs v2.2 with temp=0.0/0.6 to quantify delta.

Maya (Support): I'll reply with a workaround (temp: 0.6) and ask if they can test. Need ETA for a root cause and whether rollback is possible.

deploy-bot: rollback candidate created for model-catalog/model-v2.1 image sha256:7a3b... (artifact ready).

Liam (ML Eng): prioritizing reproduction. Initial plan: repro with node-sdk v1.4.2, same payload, compare outputs for v2.1 vs v2.2, and toggle `system_trim` flag and sampling backend. If `system_trim` is the culprit we can patch wrapper quickly.

Jenna (SRE): I'll attach full traces and request ids to the ticket and mark P1 if customer confirms production impact. Also will hold a deploy freeze on further model promotions until we patch. :eyes:

Maya (Support): thanks all. I'll update the customer with the temp workaround, notify them we have a rollback ready and that ML is reproducing. Will share results once Liam posts eval. :thumbsup:
